agendaItems.background:

The grant funds will be used for payment of overtime hours spent by Tampa Police Department officers for crime reduction initiatives to reduce community violence through a targeted, data-driven overtime initiative designed to reduce violent crime and improve public safety.

Entering into this agreement is determined to be in the best interest of the City of Tampa.

File No. PS26-28445
Resolution approving the annual submission of the Federal Equitable Sharing Agreement and Certification Report for FY end date 9/30/2026 relating to participation in the Federal Equitable Sharing Program; authorizing execution thereof by the Mayor of the City of Tampa; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background: The City of Tampa Police Department participates in numerous task forces and joint investigations with various federal law enforcement agencies.  Property and cash used to facilitate the crimes investigated jointly by said agencies are subject to forfeiture under federal law and equitably distributed among the agencies who participate in the Equitable Sharing Program with the Department of Justice.  The Federal Equitable Sharing Agreement must be submitted annually and requires a certification of the prior fiscal year funds and compliance with federal regulations.  Execution of the attached Federal Equitable Sharing Agreement and Certification is a condition of the City of Tampa’s continued participation in equitable sharing of seized property and cash.  Shared assets must be used for law enforcement purposes such as training and drug, gang and prevention awareness programs.  Entering into this agreement is determined to be in the best interest of the City of Tampa.

agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. PS26-28520 (Part 1 of 2)(See Item 5)
Resolution of the City of Tampa approving Modification No. 2 to the Federally Funded Subgrant Agreement (No. H0957) between the City of Tampa and State of Florida Division of Emergency Management for the City of Tampa, Fire Station #16, Wind Retrofit (Project No. 4486-048-R); authorizing execution thereof by the Mayor of the City of Tampa and attestation by the City Clerk; providing an effective date of October 31, 2026, nunc pro tunc.
agendaItems.background:
Modification No. 2 reinstates the Federally Funded Subgrant Agreement No. H0957and extends the period of performance to October 31, 2027, andincreases the Federal Funding by $152,335.80 for the maximum amount payable under the Agreement to $622,923.30.

It also updates the Budget and Scope of Work to reallocate funds between budget categories to align with contractor billing, provide timeline updates, and update Sub-Recipient Management Cost language. The budget has been adjusted to reallocate costs among materials, labor, and fees.

The total initial agreement amount has been updated to $692,137.00 with a Federal share of $622,923.30 and a match share of $69,213.70. In addition, this project has an estimated $34,606.00 in contingency funds ($31,145.40 federal share and $3,460.60 non-federal).

Contingency funds are not automatically available for use. Prior to their release, contingency funds must be re-budgeted to another direct cost category and identified. Post-award changes to the budget require prior written approval from the Division (FDEM). The written request should demonstrate what unforeseen conditions related to the project arose that required the use of contingency funds.

On January 23, 2026, a 20-foot section of the Picnic Island Pier collapsed into the water, resulting in the closure of the pier. agendaItems.rawTitle:
File no. NCA26-28433
Resolution of the City of Tampa, Florida, approving Amendment No. 1 to the Grant Agreement (RES15) between the City of Tampa and the Florida Department of Environmental Protection for the Picnic Island Nature-Based Solutions Project; Authorizing execution by the Mayor and attestation by the City Clerk; Providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
The grant agreement is to design nature-based solutions (NBS) at Picnic Island Park.

Amendment No. 1 deletes Attachment 1 in its entirety and replaces it with Attachment 1-A; deletes Attachment 2 in its entirety and replaces it with Attachment 2-A; deletes Attachment 3 in its entirety and replaces it with Attachment 3-A; deletes Attachment 5 in its entirety and replaces it with Attachment 5-A; and deletes Exhibit A in its entirety and replaces it with Exhibit A-1. The total funding amount of $2,000,000 is unchanged from the original agreement. There is no required match for this project.

The updates to Attachment 1-A include general formatting and updates to Section 23.

Subsection b. regarding updated references to specific civil rights laws and regulations.

The updates to Attachment 2-A include general formatting.

The updates made to Attachment 3-A include general formatting updates; adding Habitat Survey results to the Task Description for Task 2; adding not-to-exceed cost amounts for Tasks 2-5; breaking down the previous Task 4 into Task 4.1 and 4.2 to allow for more frequent reimbursement; updating the project timeline to add dates for Task 4.1 and 4.2; and updating the budget detail by task to align the budget with the project contract.

The updates to Attachment 5-A include general formatting. The updates made to Exhibit A-1 include updating Task 4 in the quarterly reporting template to include 50% for Intermediate design and adding a final project monitoring plan deliverable that had previously been left out.

This financial resolution reallocates $125,000 from the Belmont Heights Athletic Field Improvements project to the Jackson Heights Athletic Field Improvements project within the Utilities Services Tax Capital Projects Fund.

agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. INF26-28274 (Part 1 of 2)(See Item 18)
Resolution accepting the proposal of Granger Maintenance & Construction, Inc. pertaining to Contract 26-C-00003 FY26 Miscellaneous PS Riser Replacements, in the amount of $798,000; authorizing the Mayor of the City of Tampa to execute said contract on behalf of the City of Tampa; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
Background:

1. Contract Title: 26-C-00003 FY26 Miscellaneous PS Riser Replacements a. Address of Project: Various Locations b. Number of bidders/submitters: 2 (two) c.    Names of bidders/submitters: • Granger Maintenance & Construction, Inc.

• KAT Construction and Materials Inc.

d. Dollar amount: $798,000.00 e. Why the awardee was selected: The lowest responsible responsive bidder was selected pursuant to FS 255.20.

2. Contractor/Firm: Granger Maintenance & Construction, Inc.

3. Business Case: This project provides the furnish all labor, materials, and equipment for repair of 4 pumping stations including removal and replacement of existing pump bases, discharge piping, valves, and fittings, installing line-stop, bypass tee, and valves essential for bypassing the stations with all associated work required for a complete project in accordance with the Contract Documents.

4. Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement: Granger Maintenance & Construction, Inc, the prime contractor, is utilizing one (1) City of Tampa-certified firm for subcontracting.

5.    Sustainability and Resiliency: Rehabilitation of the infrastructure will restore the structural integrity, provide emergency bypassing connection, and improve pumping capacity.

The rehabilitation will extend the useful life of the pumping stations and prevent wastewater overflow at the stations.

6. Community Engagement: The Wastewater Public Relations and CAD Construction, Engineering and Inspection (CAD-CEI) team will assist the Contractor in the communication efforts to ensure transparency and integration of the stakeholders.

7. Project: a. Contract delivery method: This is a construction project.

b. Placemaking: N/A c. Time, Quality Assurance, Cost Monitoring (Budget) • 270 consecutive calendar days.

• A full-time City of Tampa Construction Inspector will be on-site during the project to ensure quality of construction.

• The e-Builder (Trimble Unity Construct) project management software system will be utilized to optimize the monitoring of schedules and costs. Trimble Unity Construct is a premier system for construction project management.

agendaItems.background:
Background:

1. Contract Title: 26-C-00046 Ybor City CRA 7th Avenue Street Resurfacing (Phase 3) a. Address of Project: Ybor City 7th Avenue, Tampa, FL 33605.

b. Number of bidders/submitters: 3 (three) c.    Names of bidders/submitters: • Cathcart Construction Company – Florida, LLC • Harris-McBurney Company • Ajax Paving Industries of Florida, LLC d. Dollar amount: $928,250.98 e.    Why the awardee was selected: The lowest qualified and responsive bidder was selected pursuant to FS 255.20.

1. Contractor/Firm: Cathcart Construction Company – Florida, LLC

2.    Business Case: This project provides for constructing pedestrian mobility and intersection improvements along 7th Avenue at the intersections of 17th Street, Angel Oliva Senior Street, and 19th Street. Work shall include clearing and grubbing, selective demolition of existing concrete improvements, tree removal, milling of existing asphalt pavement, installation of optional base, reconstruction of curb ramps at each quadrant of the intersections to achieve ADA compliance, construction of new concrete sidewalk, curb and gutter, installation of detectable warning surfaces, adjustment of existing manholes, valve boxes, and meter boxes, restoration of historic architectural brick roadway and sidewalk pavers within the project limits, installation and relocation of regulatory signing, pavement markings and raised pavement markers, relocation of existing benches, installation of new trash receptacles, and all associated restoration and incidental work necessary to complete the improvements in accordance with the Contract Documents.

b. Placemaking: N/A c.    Time, Quality Assurance, Cost Monitoring (Budget): • 90 consecutive calendar days.

• A full-time City of Tampa Construction Inspector will be on-site during the project to ensure quality  of construction.

SubjectFinancial Resolution- Realign Wastewater and Water project balances within

Resolution / 
Ordinance 
Title
A resolution making certain changes in the budget of the City of Tampa for the 
fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; approving the transfer, reallocation, 
and/or appropriation of $47,471,641.19 for use by the Wastewater and Water 
departments within the Wastewater Bonds - Series 2022 Capital Projects 
Fund, Wastewater Bonds - Series 2024 Capital Projects Fund, Water Bonds - 
Series 2022 Capital Projects Fund, and Water Bonds - Series 2024 Capital 
Projects Fund for the H. F. Curren Master Plan, Collection System 
Rehabilitation Contract, D. L. Tippin Filter Improvements, and Citywide Water 
Main Replacements projects; providing an effective date.
BACKGROUND:
This financial resolution adjusts the authorized budgets within the following water and 
wastewater bond funds:
Series 2022 – previously approved by Council and bonds have been issued
Series 2024 – previously approved by Council and bonds have been issued
This financial resolution prepares the above funds for financial closing during FY2027.   
Existing bond proceeds will be spent down by realigning FY2026 expenses from the Water 
and Wastewater Future Debt Capital Projects Funds and the Water Renewal and 
Replacement Fund with the outcome of reducing the amount of borrowed funds needed when 
the City issues the Series 2027 Water and Wastewater Bonds (formerly Water and 
Wastewater Future Debt Capital Projects Funds) scheduled during the fall of 2027.
The following summarizes the financial resolution by fund:
Wastewater Bonds – Series 2022 Capital Projects Fund
     *Appropriates $668,412.63 of Interest Earnings and Use of Fund Balance
     *Decreases various wastewater projects by $5,983,612.93
     *Increases the H.F. Curren Master Plan Project and Collection System Rehabilitation 
Contract Project by $6,652,025.56
Wastewater Bonds – Series 2024 Capital Projects Fund
     *Decreases various wastewater projects by $10,185,952.36
     *Increases the H.F. Current Master Plan Project by $9,305,809.23
     *Increases Reserves by $880,143.13

Water Bonds – Series 2022 Capital Projects Fund
     *Decreases various water projects by $14,717,685.32
     *Increases the D.L. Tippin Filter Improvements Project and the Citywide Water Main 
Replacements Project by $14,628,595.53
     *Increases Reserves by $89,090.06
Water Bonds – Series 2024 Capital Projects Fund
     *Decreases various water projects by $15,915,977.95
     *Increases the D.L. Tippin Filter Improvements Project by $14,925,191.53
*Increases reserves by $990,786.42
FISCAL IMPACT: Yes
FISCAL IMPACT STATEMENT:
This resolution realigns $6,652,025.56 from various projects within the Series 2022 
Wastewater Bonds and $10,185,952.36 from various projects within the Series 2024 
Wastewater Bonds to the H. F. Curren Master Plan Project and Collection System 
Rehabilitation Contract Project to spend down the bonds.  This resolution also realigns 
$14,717,685.32 from various projects within the Series 2022 Water Bonds to the D. L. Tippin 
Filter Improvements Project, and $15,915,977.95 from various projects within the Series 2024 
Water Bonds to the D. L. Tippin Filter Improvements Project and Citywide Water Main 
Replacements Project to spend down the bonds.

Tippin Filter Improvements Project and Citywide Water Main Replacements Project to spend down the bonds.

Resolution approving an assistance award/amendment to the Fair Housing Assistance Program Award, Instrument Number FF200KK2600034, between the City of Tampa, Florida and U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development to reimburse the City for case processing, administrative costs, and training for dually filed housing discrimination complaints by the Tampa Office of Human Rights for Fiscal Year 2026 and for training provided to City staff through June 30, 2027 in the amount of seventy-two thousand nine hundred dollars ($72,900); authorizing the execution thereof by the Mayor of the City of Tampa; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. DEO26-27675 (Part 1 of 2)(See Item 31)
Resolution approving an assistance award/amendment to the Fair Housing Assistance Program Award, Instrument Number FF200KK2600034, between the City of Tampa, Florida and U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development to reimburse the City for case processing, administrative costs, and training for dually filed housing discrimination complaints by the Tampa Office of Human Rights for Fiscal Year 2026 and for training provided to City staff through June 30, 2027 in the amount of seventy-two thousand nine hundred dollars ($72,900); authorizing the execution thereof by the Mayor of the City of Tampa; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
That the Assistance Award/Amendment to the Fair Housing Assistance Program Award, Instrument Number FF200K2600034, between the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and City of Tampa (City) for case processing, administrative costs, and training funding for dually filed housing discrimination complaints by the Tampa Office of Human Rights for Fiscal Year 2026 and for training provided to City staff through June 30, 2027, (“Award”), (a copy of which is attached hereto), is approved in its entirety or in substantially similar form.

Assistance Award/Amendment to the Fair Housing Assistance Program Award, Instrument Number FF200K2600034, the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) has contracted with the City of Tampa (City) for case processing, administrative costs, and training funding for dually filed housing discrimination complaints by the Tampa Office of Human Rights for Fiscal Year 2026 and for training provided to City staff through June 30, 2027; and pursuant to the Agreement, HUD will reimburse the City in the amount of Seventy-Two Thousand Nine Hundred Dollars ($72,900) for services rendered through the processing of housing discrimination complaints and prospective training; and the Tampa Office of Human Rights has investigated, conciliated and processed several housing discrimination complaints to conclusion; and pursuant to these services provided and verified by HUD, this amendment provides the method for payment of costs incurred by the City; and HUD has agreed to provide funding prospectively for training through June 30, 2027; and City Council does hereby affirm that it would be beneficial to the residents of the City to enter this Amendment between the City and HUD.

Title
A resolution making certain changes in the budget of the City of Tampa for the 
fiscal year ending September 30, 2027; approving the transfer, reallocation, 
and/or appropriation of $72,900 within the Housing Grants Fund for the Office 
of Human Rights Fair Housing Assistance Program (FHAP) Activities; 
providing an effective date
BACKGROUND:
The United States Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) has contracted 
with the City of Tampa (City) for case processing, administrative costs, and training funding 
for dually filed housing discrimination complaints by the Tampa Office of Human Rights for 
Fiscal Year 2026 and for training provided to City staff through June 30, 2027; and pursuant 
to the Agreement, HUD will reimburse the City in the amount of Seventy-Two Thousand Nine 
Hundred Dollars ($72,900) for services rendered through the processing of housing 
discrimination complaints and prospective training; and the Tampa Office of Human Rights 
has investigated, conciliated and processed several housing discrimination complaints to 
conclusion; and pursuant to these services provided and verified by HUD, this amendment 
provides the method for payment of costs incurred by the City; and HUD has agreed to 
provide funding prospectively for training through June 30, 2027; and City Council does 
hereby affirm that it would be beneficial to the residents of the City to enter this Amendment 
between the City and HUD.

FISCAL IMPACT STATEMENT:
The United States Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) has contracted 
with the City of Tampa for the investigation, conciliation, and other processing of dually filed 
housing discrimination complaints by the Tampa Office of Human Rights. In consideration 
thereof, HUD will contribute $72,900 to be used for conducting education and outreach to 
persons residing in the geographic area served by the Tampa Office of Human Rights. These 
funds will be deposited and appropriated within the Housing Grants Fund for such purposes.

agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. DEO26-28429
Resolution approving an agreement between the City of Tampa and Tampa Bay Wave Inc. providing local cash match support in an amount not to exceed $100,000.00 for the Tampa Bay Defense Tech Innovation Accelerator funded under U.S. Economic Development Administration Award no. ED26ATL0G0193; authorizing execution by the Mayor and attestation by the City Clerk; Providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
Tampa Bay Wave, Inc. was awarded federal financial assistance from the U.S. Department of Commerce, Economic Development Administration under Award No. ED26ATL0G0193 for the Tampa Bay Defense Tech Innovation Accelerator.  The award included a federal share of $1,377,318.00 and a recipient match of $342,000.00, for a total project cost of $1,719,318.00.

The City previously committed $100,000.00 in local cash support toward the required recipient match. Under the proposed agreement, the City will provide funding in an amount not to exceed $100,000.00 with $50,000.00 provided in Fiscal Year 2027 and $50,000.00 provided in Fiscal Year 2028.

The Tampa Bay Defense Tech Innovation Accelerator is designed to strengthen regional economic resiliency through defense technology innovation and will support two cohorts of fifteen startups each.  Program activities include accelerator programming, technical assistance, mentoring, pitch coaching, strategic introductions, access to capital, workforce development and post-cohort support.

SubjectA Resolution approving the agreement between the City of Tampa and Tampa 
Bay Wave Inc. in an amount not to exceed $100,000.00 for the Tampa Bay 
Defense Tech Innovation Accelerator funded under U.S. Economic 
Development Administration Award.
Resolution / 
Ordinance 
Title
A Resolution approving an agreement between the City of Tampa and Tampa 
Bay Wave Inc. providing local cash match support in an amount not to exceed 
$100,000.00 for the Tampa Bay Defense Tech Innovation Accelerator funded 
under U.S. Economic Development Administration Award no. 
ED26ATL0G0193; authorizing execution by the Mayor and attestation by the 
City Clerk; Providing an effective date.
BACKGROUND:
Tampa Bay Wave, Inc. was awarded federal financial assistance from the U.S. Department of 
Commerce, Economic Development Administration under Award No. ED26ATL0G0193 for 
the Tampa Bay Defense Tech Innovation Accelerator.  The award included a federal share of 
$1,377,318.00 and a recipient match of $342,000.00, for a total project cost of $1,719,318.00. 
The City previously committed $100,000.00 in local cash support toward the required 
recipient match. Under the proposed agreement, the City will provide funding in an amount 
not to exceed $100,000.00 with $50,000.00 provided in Fiscal Year 2027 and $50,000.00 
provided in Fiscal Year 2028. 
The Tampa Bay Defense Tech Innovation Accelerator is designed to strengthen regional 
economic resiliency through defense technology innovation and will support two cohorts of 
fifteen startups each.  Program activities include accelerator programming, technical 
assistance, mentoring, pitch coaching, strategic introductions, access to capital, workforce 
development and post-cohort support.
FISCAL IMPACT: Yes
FISCAL IMPACT STATEMENT:
That the City of Tampa shall provide financial support in an amount $50,000 in FY2027 and 
$50,000 in FY2028, subject to appropriation, not to exceed a total of $100,000.00, as local 
cash match for eligible costs of the Tampa Bay Defense Tech Innovation Accelerator under 
EDA Award No. ED26ATL0G0193, subject to the terms, documentation requirements and 
funding availability set forth in the Agreement. Funding for such is from Development and 
Economic Opportunity within the General Fund.
PROJECTED COSTS: 01100.213700.582531 $50,000 (Expenditure)

File No. MAM26-28522
Resolution authorizing an Agreement for Consultant Services in the amount of $900,000 between the City of Tampa and Mead and Hunt, Inc. in connection with Contract 26-D-00011 Smart Mobility General Engineering Contract; authorizing the Mayor of the City of Tampa to execute same; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. MAM26-28522
Resolution authorizing an Agreement for Consultant Services in the amount of $900,000 between the City of Tampa and Mead and Hunt, Inc. in connection with Contract 26-D-00011 Smart Mobility General Engineering Contract; authorizing the Mayor of the City of Tampa to execute same; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
1. Background: a. Contract Title: Smart Mobility General Engineering Contract b. Address of Project: Various locations throughout the City c. Number of bidders/submitters: Five (5) d.    Names of bidders/submitters: •EJB Engineering, LLC • HBC Engineering Company • Iteris, Inc •Kimley-Horn and Associates, Inc.

•Mead and Hunt, Inc.

2.  Dollar amount: $900,000.00

2.    Why the awardee was selected: Selected Pursuant to FS 287.055 CCNA.

3. Contractor/Firm: Mead and Hunt, Inc.

4.    Business Case:  This Agreement provides for a wide range of professional engineering services to assist the Mobility Department with the Smart Mobility program. Project  will support innovative techniques and best practices that will maximize the value and effectiveness of this technology, enhance operational performance, and improve overall system outcomes.

Services will include, but not limited to: advancing Safety, Mobility, Automated, Real-time Traffic Management (SMART) Corridor monitoring, assisting in identifying data sources for best practices in congestion management, assessing Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) and detection device features with optimizing applications, developing prioritization tools for traffic signal installation, upgrades, and removals, identifying passive detection locations for the bicycle network, and other technical support as needed.

This is a three (3) year contract, project will be managed through a series of subsequently issued task orders.

5. Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement: Mead and Hunt, Inc., the prime contractor, is committed to utilizing two (2) city-certified firms for subcontracting.

6. Sustainability and Resiliency: This project is consistent with Transforming Tampa's Tomorrow goal of Sustainability and Resiliency and is integral to the Smart Mobility program.

Community Engagement: The Mobility Department staff will assist the Firm in the communication efforts to ensure transparency and integration of the stakeholders.

7. Project: a.    Contract delivery method: This is a Design-Bid- Build project.

b. Placemaking: N/A c. Time, Quality Assurance, Cost Monitoring (Budget) •  365 consecutive calendar days.

• The e-Builder project management software system will be utilized to optimize the monitoring of schedules and costs. This software was recently purchased by the City of Tampa and is a premier system for construction project management.

Resolution setting a public hearing for December 10, 2026 at 5:01 P.M., or as soon thereafter, in City Council Chambers, 315 E. Kennedy Blvd., 3rd Floor, Tampa, FL 33602, before Tampa City Council to consider the draft Consolidated Annual Performance and Evaluation Report to The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development regarding the City’s Community Development Block Grant, Emergency Solutions Grant, Home Investment Partnerships, and Housing Opportunities For Persons With Aids Programs for the 2025 Program and 2026 Fiscal Year that ended on September 30, 2026; Providing an Effective Date.
agendaItems.background:
The City of Tampa is the recipient of federal funds under Title I of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974 (PL 93-383) from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (“HUD”) for the City’s Community Development Block Grant, Emergency Solutions Grant, HOME Investment Partnerships and Housing Opportunities for Persons with AIDS Programs. The City is required by federal law and regulations to provide a Consolidated Annual Performance and Evaluation Report (“CAPER”) to HUD summarizing the activities undertaken and the progress achieved in the Programs during the 2025 Program/2026 Fiscal Year that ended on September 30, 2026.

File No. PH26-27129
Public hearing to consider whether to opt-out of the property tax exemption for certain multifamily projects that provide affordable housing in the 80% - 120% range of the median annual adjusted gross income, which properties would otherwise be eligible for an exemption from ad valorem taxation pursuant to Section 196.1978(3)(d)1.a., Florida Statutes. (Motion adopting resolution to schedule said public hearing initiated by Maniscalco-Miranda on October 15, 2026)
Resolution adopted by the City of Tampa, Florida, pursuant to Subsection 196.1978(3)(o), Florida Statutes, electing to "Opt-Out" of the property tax exemption for certain multifamily projects that provide affordable housing in the 80%-120% range of median annual adjusted gross income, which properties would otherwise be eligible for an exemption from ad valorem taxation pursuant to Subsection 196.1978(3)(D)1.a, Florida Statutes; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. PH26-27129
Public hearing to consider whether to opt-out of the property tax exemption for certain multifamily projects that provide affordable housing in the 80% - 120% range of the median annual adjusted gross income, which properties would otherwise be eligible for an exemption from ad valorem taxation pursuant to Section 196.1978(3)(d)1.a., Florida Statutes. (Motion adopting resolution to schedule said public hearing initiated by Maniscalco-Miranda on October 15, 2026)
Resolution adopted by the City of Tampa, Florida, pursuant to Subsection 196.1978(3)(o), Florida Statutes, electing to "Opt-Out" of the property tax exemption for certain multifamily projects that provide affordable housing in the 80%-120% range of median annual adjusted gross income, which properties would otherwise be eligible for an exemption from ad valorem taxation pursuant to Subsection 196.1978(3)(D)1.a, Florida Statutes; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
Section 196.1978(3), Florida Statutes, requires the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser to exempt certain qualifying rental properties from ad valorem taxation when such properties meet the statutory criteria for multifamily projects that provide affordable housing to households within specified income limits. Section 196.1978(3)(d)1.a. of the Florida Statutes provides a 75% ad valorem tax exemption es (i.e. 75% of the assessed property value is exempt from property taxes)  for affordable housing that serves persons or families whose annual household income is greater than 80 percent but not more than 120 percent of the median annual adjusted gross income ("AMI")  for households within that metropolitan statistical area("MSA").

However, in its 2024 session, the Florida Legislature adopted a bill (HB 7073, Laws of Florida Ch. 2024-158)  that allows taxing authorities such as the City of Tampa to annually "opt-out" of providing that exemption if the three previous years Shimberg Center for Housing Studies Annual Reports which are prepared at the University of Florida per Sec. 420.6075, Florida Statutes ("Shimberg Annual Reports") determine that the number of available afforable units is an MSA is greater than the number of renter households in the MSA for the category entitled 0-120% AMI.  It is necessary to hold a public hearing on the proposed resolution to receive public comment and allow the Tampa City Council to consider whether to approve the proposed opt-out of the 80–120 Tax Exemption.

This renewal occurs in three-year intervals and is necessary to license these systems for ongoing use. If the subscription lapses, expires or otherwise is not renewed, access to the city applications, email and data will cease.

The City desires to renew the Microsoft Enterprise Enrollment for Software Assurance and Subscription Licenses allowing for the direct purchase of the Microsoft Licenses and Products from Microsoft’s reseller, CDW Government, LLC. through the State of Florida Contract #43230000-23-NASPO-ACS for Microsoft License, Maintenance, and Services.
